title: Drishyam 3 Out-Earns First Two Films Combined as Franchise Crosses Rs 1,000 Crore
excerpt: Koimoi puts the Hindi thriller at Rs 578.64 crore worldwide after 24 days, taking the three-film total to Rs 1,028.17 crore, while Sacnilk-based tracking puts the film lower at Rs 572.45 crore.
body:
• Koimoi puts Drishyam 3 at Rs 578.64 crore worldwide gross after 24 days, more than Drishyam (Rs 109.64 crore) and Drishyam 2 (Rs 339.89 crore) combined at Rs 449.53 crore.
  • On Koimoi's figures the three Hindi films total Rs 1,028.17 crore worldwide, taking the franchise past Rs 1,000 crore.
  • Trackers differ on the exact total: Sacnilk-based reporting in The Times of India put day-24 worldwide gross at Rs 572.45 crore, with the gap concentrated in overseas estimates.
  • Koimoi lists the film's budget at Rs 110 crore, India net at Rs 369.3 crore and overseas gross at Rs 142.94 crore.

Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3: The Conclusion has out-earned its two predecessors combined and pushed the Hindi Drishyam franchise past Rs 1,000 crore worldwide, according to Koimoi's day-24 report. The film, directed by Abhishek Pathak and starring Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar alongside Tabu, is a Hindi crime thriller and the closing chapter of the trilogy.

The milestone in numbers

Koimoi reported a worldwide gross of Rs 578.64 crore after 24 days, made up of Rs 435.80 crore gross in India on a net collection of Rs 369.30 crore, plus Rs 142.94 crore overseas. That single-film total exceeds the combined lifetime worldwide gross of Drishyam at Rs 109.64 crore and Drishyam 2 at Rs 339.89 crore, which together stand at Rs 449.53 crore. Koimoi put the difference at almost Rs 130 crore and listed the franchise total as Rs 1,028.17 crore, with Drishyam 3 accounting for more than half of it.

"Either way, the central record is not in dispute between the sources: Drishyam 3 alone has earned more than the first two films combined, and the franchise total is now above Rs 1,000 crore."

The film is also closing on the next round number. At Rs 578.64 crore it sits Rs 21.36 crore short of Rs 600 crore worldwide, a mark Koimoi said it is moving towards as its fourth week continues.

Why the totals differ between trackers

Readers will see a lower headline figure elsewhere, and the difference matters. Reporting based on Sacnilk estimates, carried by The Times of India, put the day-24 worldwide gross at Rs 572.45 crore. That report gave India net at Rs 368.90 crore and India gross at Rs 441.95 crore, broadly in line with Koimoi on the domestic side, but overseas gross at Rs 130.50 crore, well below Koimoi's Rs 142.94 crore. In other words, the two trackers agree the film is in the Rs 570 crore range and that the franchise has crossed Rs 1,000 crore on either count when the earlier films are added; they disagree mainly on how much has been counted overseas so far.

The Times of India report also tracked the shape of the run. It said the film collected Rs 3 crore net in India on its fourth Sunday, October 25, up 13.2% from Rs 2.65 crore on Saturday, across 2,877 shows, and sold 142,277 tickets that day for a cumulative 15,908,406 tickets. Its week-wise split was Rs 245.50 crore in week one, Rs 87.50 crore in week two and Rs 28.85 crore in week three on a net basis.

A low-budget franchise outlier

Koimoi listed the production budget at Rs 110 crore, with profit of Rs 259.3 crore and a return of 235.73% on its summary. Those economics explain why the milestone carries weight beyond the headline total: this is not a franchise built on ever-larger spectacle budgets. The Drishyam films have grown on the strength of a single character, Vijay Salgaonkar, and a story audiences have followed across three releases, with each sequel substantially out-grossing the film before it, from Rs 109.64 crore to Rs 339.89 crore and now to the Rs 570 crore-plus range.

What it means for diaspora audiences

The overseas share is the part of the story most relevant outside India. Even on the lower Sacnilk-based estimate, overseas gross had reached Rs 130.50 crore by day 24, and on Koimoi's count Rs 142.94 crore, underlining that a Hindi thriller without a conventional action spectacle has held screens in international markets for four weeks. For diaspora viewers, the run offers a useful counterpoint to the assumption that only large-scale event films travel: word of mouth around a familiar franchise title has sustained this release well past its opening weekend.

What to watch next

The next test is whether the film reaches Rs 600 crore worldwide before its theatrical run winds down, and whether final overseas reporting closes the gap between the tracker estimates. Either way, the central record is not in dispute between the sources: Drishyam 3 alone has earned more than the first two films combined, and the franchise total is now above Rs 1,000 crore.
